summary: Finite first-write audit confirms all three legacy REVIEW_RESULT events in the event-compat set have already been rewritten on authoritative swarm-control. Authority moved top-level review coordinates into metadata; cart moved top-level slotId into metadata; WorldEntity lost top-level pr/headSha/verdict=SYNC_REQUIRED without a metadata replacement. Their current Git blob identities differ from audited first-write blobs. MaterialDNA remains byte-exact. Any compatibility repair that validates strict current bytes first will ratify already-proven immutable-history corruption; recovery must pin audited original blobs and safely restore the three known laundered current blobs to those exact originals under a one-way exact transition or stronger trusted-history mechanism.

Cart first-write 6b2b7e087b4e7fa67fd3b0ed9724cae7cb542808 blob a39220b473086229e6b1057b296342175b851af1 contains top-level slotId='audit'; current swarm-control blob 162e42ab9ab08e7976d61e78ad12bbd088ff13a8 moves slotId under metadata.

The earlier live laundering repro proved a failed immutable rewrite can remain as branch tip and become a later PASS baseline, explaining why these current blobs cannot be trusted merely because generic strict validation accepts them.
PR #329 comment 5250976045 records the exact blob matrix and a bounded restoration recommendation.
